critique.point: qualm judges each file as a whole, but reviewers point at one spot. push_back gives one overall probability per file, while real requests to simplify are anchored on one line or block. That mismatch explains why the baseline fails far fewer reviewer positives than injected smells.
critique.evidence: builtin.json push_back; benchmark_summary: reviewer positives are 'usually about one spot in an otherwise fine change; many are small'; baseline fails 16% of reviewer positives vs 64% of injected smells; in dev_examples, 6 of 8 reviewer locations are a single line and the widest is 16 lines.

critique.point: The gap between the 16% and the 64% is mainly caused by that mismatch in scale. A large, mostly fine new unit with one redundant construct (for example `return await`) scores low when judged whole.
critique.evidence: dev_examples #6 (return await in a small hook), #2 (redundant parens in a 57-line new function); the gap in baseline fail rates.

critique.point: Jev never sees the context that reviewers and qualm's own questions rely on. The state is the diff with 8 lines of context, so 'already in the file' and 'the surrounding code shows' are asked about code Jev mostly cannot see. The full head file is in the repository and qualm does not read it.
critique.evidence: internal/gitdiff/gitdiff.go:283-285 (-U8); builtin.json wording of added_copies and added_impossible_guards; dev_examples #4 (the other branch), #1 (expr handles it), #7 (16 callers).

critique.point: push_back tells Jev to set comments and documentation aside, which throws away evidence a reviewer used.
critique.evidence: builtin.json push_back text; dev_examples #3, where the reviewer cites the docstring as proof the check is useless.

critique.point: Two of the five things reviewers ask for have no question: reuse (the library, the language or an existing helper already does this) and shortening a redundant construct. Parallel paths and code with no effect are covered only by stretching added_impossible_guards. Spike questions that matched reviewer behaviour (pass_through_layers, added_tangle, noise_comments) did not ship.
critique.evidence: dev_examples #8 (use Instant/Duration), #2 and #6 (redundant constructs), #4 (unify two branches), #3 (a check that only logs); spike/questions.json and spike/questions-change.json vs internal/questions/builtin.json.

critique.point: About half of the ten questions feed neither the gate nor the fix. comments_only and grew_a_big_unit can be computed deterministically, and added_placeholders is a regex job. new_behaviour cannot clear a change because almost every positive is new behaviour, and direction and simplified overlap with push_back.
critique.evidence: builtin.json roles; only push_back gates (contract/questions Q1); the injected debug_print and placeholder smells are mechanical (next/collect/mechanical.py).

critique.point: The report does not say where the problem is or what to do. Each diagnosis points at the whole hunk where it is strongest, so in the README's own example three diagnoses all point at lines 327-577, and every finding's fix is the generic 'Rework the change so this no longer applies.'

critique.point: The 0.6 threshold was chosen to keep the fail rate low on one unlabelled Ruby repository, not to agree with reviewers. On the trial sample it gives recall of only 0.33.
critique.evidence: Design doc and README 'How the gate was chosen' (blocked 2 of 99 commits); benchmark_summary precision 0.71 / recall 0.33 at 0.6.

critique.point: False alarms on single files add up across a PR, because one failing file fails the whole PR. At 4-14% false fails per clean file, a clean ten-file PR is blocked 34-78% of the time. The gate needs about a 2% per-file false-fail rate and a distinction between nits and blocking requests.
critique.evidence: contract/gate G1; benchmark_summary clean-negative fail rates 4% and 14%; arithmetic 1-(0.96^10) and 1-(0.86^10).

critique.point: The labels are noisy exactly where the signal is. Two of the eight sampled reviewer positives are not requests to simplify (praise, and a correctness question matched by the WEAK pattern 'duplicate'), and nits count as positive. Whether a reviewer flags a nit depends on the project, which caps the PR-AUC any tool can reach against real reviewers.
critique.evidence: dev_examples #1 ('nice catch! Great to not have duplicate logic'), #5 ('Were ids reused... duplicate docs'); next/collect/simplify_regex.py WEAK pattern; benchmark_summary 'Known label noise'.

candidates.name: R1-spot-review
candidates.one_line: Judge each changed unit (function, method or top-level block) with its whole text, its base version and a file outline. Ask Jev which of five verbs (remove, reuse, merge, shorten, split) a reviewer would apply, add deterministic detectors, and combine everything in a calibrated logistic model.
candidates.design: Computes: the units that enclose each hunk in the head file, found by indentation and braces as next/collect/mechanical.py does, each matched to its base version by name, with lengths and nesting depth before and after. Winnowing fingerprints (k=5, window 4) over identifier-normalised tokens of every head file in the change. Regex detectors for debug output and TODO stubs (a TODO with a bug link or owner is exempt). Flags for changes that are clean by construction: comments only, formatting, rename, move. Asks: one Jev request per changed unit, at most 12 per file. The state is the unit's head and base text, a one-line-per-signature outline of the file, and the hunk. Questions: would_comment (would a reviewer leave an inline comment asking for this code to be removed, reused, merged, shortened or split?), one yes/no question per verb, impossible_guard and unused_option. Comments count as evidence. Decides: logistic regression over about 15 features (max and noisy-OR of would_comment across spots, max per verb, detector hits, copy similarity, unit growth, size, clean-change flags), fitted with repository-grouped cross-validation and isotonic calibration. The threshold is set for a 2% fail rate on clean negatives. A close call re-asks only the deciding spot and takes the median of three. Reports: per finding, the spot's own lines (both halves of a copy via related), the verb, a message built from deterministic facts, and a fix specific to the verb.
candidates.hypothesis: The baseline misses reviewer positives because it judges whole files with too little context, not because of Jev. Judging each spot with its full context, using the verbs reviewers actually use, raises recall on reviewer positives without losing precision.
candidates.falsify: On dev with repository-grouped cross-validation, any one of these: (1) at the baseline's precision (0.71), R1 does not fail at least 10 points more Tier-A reviewer positives than the baseline; (2) R1's PR-AUC on reviewer items (reviewer_comment against approved negatives) is not at least 0.05 higher; (3) the ablation shows the verb questions add less than 0.02 PR-AUC over spot-level would_comment alone, meaning the scale of judgement is everything and the verbs are decoration.
candidates.est_cost_per_pr_usd: 0.004 (about 10k Jev tokens per file, ten-file PR), 2-3 s

candidates.name: R2-staff-reviewer-on-band
candidates.one_line: Run R1 on every file. Send only files whose verdict is uncertain to a cheap LLM reviewer that writes at most three inline comments, check each comment deterministically, and fail the file on any verified blocking comment.
candidates.design: R1 settles every file outside an abstain band. The band is set by conformal risk control so that at most 2% of dev decisions outside it are wrong. Each file inside the band gets one call to a Claude Haiku-class model, with the head file (capped at 8k tokens around the changed units), the diff and the outline. The model returns at most three comments, each with lines, verb, blocking or nit, quoted code and a replacement. The tool checks each comment: the quote must appear in the added lines, and the replacement must be shorter or delete lines. Comments that fail are dropped, which also defeats instructions planted in code comments. The file fails on any verified blocking comment, and the report is the verified comments. Determinism: temperature 0, and the verdict depends only on the blocking flags. If two calls disagree, the file is judged on the union of their blocking comments.
candidates.hypothesis: An LLM reviewer writes the comment a person would, which gives better ranking on real reviewer items and better fix-loop success. Keeping it to the uncertain band gets most of that gain for about a fifth of the cost.
candidates.falsify: On the 150-item dev subset, any one of these: R2 beats R1 by less than 0.05 PR-AUC on reviewer items; its fix-loop success is no higher than R1's; or its verdicts flip on more than 1% of files across repeated runs.
candidates.est_cost_per_pr_usd: under 0.01 (R1 cost plus about $0.002 per file in the band, if about 20% of files land there)

candidates.name: C1 Pinpoint
candidates.one_line: Jev asked per changed unit plus exact and evasion detectors, combined by a calibrated logistic regression. Findings carry exact lines, a named counterpart, a fix and a checkable 'done when' tied to the gate.
candidates.design: Computes: changed units in base and head by indentation and braces (as in mechanical.py unit_end), each with its diff slice and sizes. Exact detectors: debug output, placeholder stubs, a guard on a value constructed within 5 lines, unit growth (a unit of 40+ lines grown by 10+), and near-copies by winnowing across all changed files and the base file, which supplies 'related'. Evasion detectors: config, keep, .gitattributes or CI changes in the PR; a rename judged by the stricter of its old and new path; fingerprints of added lines in skipped files matched against judged files (8+ lines fails); text addressed to the tool in comments or strings. Asks: one Jev request per changed unit (push_back plus five diagnoses) plus the baseline's file-level request, the latter also sent with comment lines stripped, taking the higher score. Decides: a logistic regression over file push_back, max unit push_back, units at 0.5 or above, max diagnosis, detector flags, size and a new-file flag, Platt-calibrated on dev, with the threshold set at the baseline's precision. Exact and evasion detectors block whatever the score. Config and keeps are read from the base commit. Reports: per finding, exact lines with the first one quoted, a one-sentence why, a fix naming the counterpart, and 'done when' (line gone, blocks share under half their tokens, unit back to its old size, unit score under the threshold). Each failing file says which findings, once resolved, bring it under the threshold (regression features zeroed). The report never prints the keep command; it says to ask a person. Costs about $0.001 per PR, under 5 s.
candidates.hypothesis: Fix-loop failures come from imprecise reports that don't match the gate, not from the score. Asking per unit recovers the local reviewer asks that a whole-file question dilutes. Reading config from the base and detecting evasions handles every config, skip and attribute attack.
candidates.falsify: First-iteration fix-loop success not above the baseline's (95% CI of the difference includes zero); or the finding-line hit rate on labelled locations (within 3 lines) not above the baseline's hunk ranges at a smaller median span; or an ablation without the unit features with equal reviewer-comment PR-AUC on dev; or any config, skip or attribute red-team attack passing.

candidates.name: C2 Reviewer's note
candidates.one_line: C1's verdict unchanged. For each file C1 fails, one Haiku-class LLM call writes a reviewer-style comment and a suggested replacement hunk per finding, so LLM variance can never flip the verdict.
candidates.design: Only files that C1 failed go to the LLM, with the diff, the unit slices and C1's findings with their lines. For each finding the LLM writes one reviewer-style sentence and a replacement unified-diff hunk of at most 30 lines that preserves behaviour. Alternatively it marks the finding doubtful, which is shown to a person and never passes the file. The verdict and 'done when' stay C1's. Haiku 5.5 rejects non-default sampling settings, so temperature 0 is not available as a fix, which is why the LLM never decides. About 6K tokens per failing file at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens comes to under $0.002 per failing file. In this study the LLM call is made through the --llm-dir subagent mechanism.
candidates.hypothesis: A concrete suggested patch raises first-try fix success on idiom and redundancy findings (return await, redundant parens, Instant/Duration), where a template can't say what to write.
candidates.falsify: Fix-loop success not at least 5 points above C1's on the same items; or accepted suggested patches break tests or behaviour more often than the agent's own fixes under C1.

predictions: qualm 0.1.1 passes (fails to catch) at least 6 of these 8 attacks: a self-added keep, gate threshold 1 in qualm.json, push_back redefined in qualm.json, skip ['*'] in qualm.json, linguist-generated in .gitattributes, code moved under test/ or vendor/, a rename to *.generated.*, and a CI workflow edit adding --threshold. C1 catches all 8.

On the baseline's failing files, the median reported line range exceeds 40 lines, and in at least 30% of them every fired diagnosis points at the same range. C1's median finding span is 12 lines or fewer, with an equal or higher hit rate on labelled locations (within 3 lines).

At least half of the baseline's fix-loop failures end in one of two ways: tests pass and every reported diagnosis is below 0.5 while push_back stays at or above 0.6, or the failing file had no diagnosis reported at all.

Any candidate whose verdict depends on a single LLM sample per file (no vote, no deterministic band, caches off) exceeds the 1% verdict flip-rate limit. Candidates that use the LLM only to write the report stay within it.

Exact detectors (debug print, placeholder, near-copy, impossible guard) lift the fail rate on injected smells from 64% to at least 90%, with at most 2 points more failures on clean and hard negatives. They change reviewer-comment PR-AUC by less than 0.03.
C2's LLM-suggested patches raise first-iteration fix-loop success by less than 5 points over C1's report. Once the coding agent knows where, why and what 'done' means, it writes the fix itself.

candidates.name: M1-calibrated-stack
candidates.one_line: Jev's ten logits plus cheap deterministic diff features, stacked by a repo-grouped cross-fitted logistic regression, thresholded at a matched FPR, with a noise-measured sequential re-ask and a deterministic tiebreak
candidates.design: Per file: log added/removed lines, growth of the largest touched unit (indent/brace units), added nesting depth, within-file near-copy similarity via winnowed fingerprints, generic leftover tokens (print/console/TODO/not-implemented), guards on just-assigned values, comment/whitespace/rename-only flags, language. If the logit is within 2.5 measured sigma of the threshold, re-ask Jev up to 4 more times and average logits; if still inside, a Jev-free feature model decides (deterministic). Report: each fired feature as a finding with exact lines and related lines for copies, Jev diagnoses localized by hunk, confidence = out-of-fold precision of the finding.

candidates.one_line: A gate that runs offline with no model. Lexical detectors and winnowing clone detection feed a sign-constrained, size-controlled logistic regression over excess-structure features computed from the full base and head files.
candidates.design: Computes: a lexer per language family (C-like, Python, Ruby); added lines from a pinned git diff -U0; units from header regexes with extent by braces, indentation or a matching 'end'. Features: size controls (log1p of added, deleted and head code lines; hunk count); regret = sum over grown units of [(s+g)^1.5 - s^1.5 - g^1.5]/50^1.5, the convex cost of not extracting; class_growth; dcog (growth in SonarSource cognitive complexity per touched unit, Go err idiom counted 0); dnest; copy (winnowing, k=12 normalized tokens, w=8, IDF-weighted containment, returns both spans); single_use and pass_through (MDL); log_only; lexical detectors (debug output of a kind absent from the base, TODO in a stub body, null test right after construction, commented-out code, redundant idioms); exact zeros for whitespace-only, comment-only, rename and move. Asks nothing. Decides: a detector or copy > 0.8 with dev precision >= 0.9 fails the file directly. Otherwise a logistic regression with non-negative smell coefficients, language intercepts and the size controls, fitted with repository-grouped CV and Platt-calibrated out of fold. The threshold is the lowest with out-of-fold precision >= 0.75, with a conformal per-PR false-fail check. Report: exact added-line spans (never context), the related span for a copy, a message with numbers, a templated fix, and dev precision as confidence. Cost: $0, under 1 s, flip rate 0.
candidates.hypothesis: Excess structure measured deterministically from the full files predicts reviewer pushback at least as well as Jev reading the diff, and its signal is not just size.
candidates.falsify: On dev items that are not injected (grouped CV), T1's PR-AUC is below the baseline's with the bootstrap CI of the difference entirely below 0, or T1 beats a size-only logistic model by less than 0.02 PR-AUC.

candidates.name: T2-jev-plus-metrics
candidates.one_line: One Jev request per file. All ten answers, as logits, are stacked with T1's features in the same constrained, calibrated model. Localization comes deterministically from T1's spans, with no hunk-by-hunk pass.
candidates.design: Computes T1's features and asks Jev once per file, as qualm 0.1.1 does. The ten answers are logit-transformed and enter the logistic regression with T1's features. T1's lexical layer stays as a floor that no text in the diff can lower. The where-pass requests are dropped: findings come from T1's detectors, and diagnoses that only Jev fires attach to the unit with the largest regret or dcog. A close call is re-asked only when the combined score is within 3 * beta_jev * sigma_jev of the threshold, where sigma_jev is Jev's measured logit spread over identical calls. Threshold and calibration are chosen as in T1. Report: as T1, plus Jev diagnoses as messages on deterministic spans. Cost: about $0.0003 per PR, under a few seconds.
candidates.hypothesis: Jev (idiom, intent) and the deterministic metrics (the whole file, exactly) make complementary errors, so stacking them beats either one alone.
candidates.falsify: T2 does not beat the baseline's PR-AUC on dev items that are not injected (the CI of the difference includes 0), so its whole gain is the injected smells T1 alone catches. Or Jev's coefficient falls to about 0 once the metrics are in the model.

predictions: On mechanical injections, T1 (pure deterministic) fails at least 95% of injected files and at most 3% of their clean twins. The baseline stays near 64%.

A size-only logistic model (log added, deleted and head code lines, plus language) reaches ROC-AUC >= 0.65 on dev items that are not injected. Among negatives, push_back has a Spearman correlation >= 0.3 with log added code lines.
On dev items that are not injected, T1 does not beat the baseline's PR-AUC. T2 beats it by at least 0.03, but on reviewer_comment items alone T2's gain is under 0.03 and its CI includes 0.
On pairs of a reviewer positive and its post_fix version, no deterministic feature reaches a paired AUC of 0.60, and neither does Jev's push_back.

The ablation keeps the lexical detectors, copy, regret and dnest. Removing Halstead, change entropy or compression novelty nu changes grouped-CV PR-AUC by less than 0.005, and nu correlates with winnowing copy at Spearman >= 0.7 on blocks of at least 500 bytes.

T1's and T2's median finding width is at most a fifth of the baseline's. Under the current slack-2 overlap rule the baseline's localization hit rate is within 10 points of theirs, but under IoU >= 0.2 they beat it by at least 20 points. Swapping in tree-sitter for unit detection moves PR-AUC by less than 0.01.

critique.point: Fork PRs are never gated: qualm's own CI runs --dry-run when there is no secret, and a dry run exits 0. Any design that needs a key must either block outside contributors or skip them.
critique.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml, 'self' job (dry-run fallback); internal/cli/cli.go:195 (`if res.DryRun || res.Passed()` returns exit 0); the design doc puts a GitHub Action out of scope.

critique.point: Policy is read from the PR being judged. A PR can raise the threshold, redefine push_back, skip every file, mark itself linguist-generated or binary, or keep its own change. CODEOWNERS is the only mitigation, and it sits outside qualm.
critique.evidence: internal/check/run.go calls config.Load(o.Dir) on the working tree. gitdiff.go runs `check-attr` on the working tree. Binary detection keys on git's 'Binary files' line and no --text is passed (gitdiff.go:246). The README says to put qualm.json and .gitattributes behind review. Seven red-team attacks target this (self_keep, config_*, gitattributes_*, cache_poison).

critique.point: The answer cache is trusted without a signature and sits in the user cache dir by default, where any earlier CI step that runs PR code can plant a passing entry. In CI the cache saves almost nothing.
critique.evidence: internal/jev/cache.go (Get trusts any well-formed entry); README: 'qualm trusts what it finds in its cache'; benchmark_summary: about $0.0003 per change. That teams usually run tests before qualm in the same job is an assumption.

critique.point: The documented CI recipe (full-history clone plus go install @latest) costs far more in runner time than Jev does, and @latest lets the gate change without a commit.
critique.evidence: The README 'In CI' snippet uses fetch-depth: 0 and `go install ...@latest`. A runner-minute estimate at 30,000 runs a month is hundreds of dollars, against about $9 of Jev.

critique.point: An outage or a hung endpoint makes every check red and takes about 6 minutes to fail, well over the 60 s p95 budget, on an endpoint marked alpha. This is the most likely reason a team turns it off in the first week.
critique.evidence: internal/jev/client.go: http.Client timeout of 90 s per attempt, 4 attempts, backoff of 1+2+4 s, Endpoint https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions. README: 'It never passes a change it couldn't judge.'

critique.point: False positives per file compound into false blocks per PR: at 4% per file a clean 6-file PR fails about 22% of the time, and at 14% about 60%. The study's per-file metrics hide what a team actually feels.
critique.evidence: benchmark_summary: 4% fail rate on approved negatives and 14% on survived_90d; 1-0.96^6 = 0.22 and 1-0.86^6 = 0.60.

critique.point: Findings are hard to act on: hunk-wide line ranges, the question's text as the message, and a fixed fix sentence. Finding those ranges costs an extra request per hunk.
critique.evidence: The README's example points three diagnoses at lines 327-577. next/candidates/a-baseline/adapt.py sets the fix to 'Rework the change so this no longer applies.' internal/check/where.go asks once per hunk.

critique.point: The single static binary with no dependencies (gem, go install, release binaries) and exit codes 0/1/2 shared with exhale are real DevEx strengths. Python, cgo/tree-sitter, a model runtime or a second vendor must each pay for losing them.
critique.evidence: README Install; release.yml builds a gem per platform. That cgo would break cross-compilation of the release is an assumption.

critique.point: Diffs go to two third parties (OpenRouter, then TypeSafe), so enterprises need a vendor review and air-gapped teams cannot use qualm at all.
critique.evidence: README 'What leaves your machine'. The effect on enterprise adoption is an assumption.

candidates.name: O+J offline-first two-tier gate
candidates.one_line: Deterministic Go features with exact-line findings, plus an optional single Jev request, combined in a two-weight-set calibrated logistic regression that falls back to offline-only when there is no key.
candidates.design: Computes per file, offline (about 10 ms): exact pass classes (whitespace-only, comments-only, rename-only, move); line-precise detectors for debug output, placeholder stubs (not plain TODO comments), near-copies by winnowing over normalised token k-grams against the rest of the file and the PR's other files, growth of a long unit found by indentation, and added nesting and branches; size and shape features. If OPENROUTER_API_KEY is set, it sends one Jev request per file with push_back, added_impossible_guards and added_unused_flexibility, and skips the hunk-by-hunk pass. Decides with logistic regression using two weight sets (with Jev and without), each fit on repository-grouped dev folds, Platt-calibrated and embedded in the binary as JSON, at an operating point with precision of at least 0.71. With no key or Jev down it uses the offline weights and the report says so. The report gives exact lines, related ranges for copies (including in other files), a concrete message and a specific fix. Cost is $0 offline and about $0.0002 per PR with Jev, p95 under 3 s. It ships with --policy-from base, label-based keeps in CI, no cache in CI, and a pull_request_target Action.
candidates.hypothesis: Offline features carry the signal on injected smells and hard negatives, and Jev carries the reviewer-comment signal. One calibrated model over both beats either alone, and the offline weights alone are good enough to gate fork and air-gapped PRs.
candidates.falsify: Falsified if the Jev weights do not beat the baseline's PR-AUC with the CI of the difference above zero; or if removing the offline features costs less than 0.01 PR-AUC (then ship Jev plus the platform fixes only); or if the offline weights fall below 0.71 precision at recall of 0.2 or more, or fail more than 1% of hard negatives.

candidates.name: R-LLM: the LLM writes the report, never the verdict
candidates.one_line: An add-on: one Haiku 5.5 call per failing file rewrites the findings into at most three validated {lines, message, fix}, without touching the verdict.
candidates.design: After the winning verdict model settles, each failing file (about 15% of files) gets one Haiku 5.5 call with the diff, the units the deterministic findings point at, and those findings. It returns at most three findings; any whose lines are not added lines is dropped and the templated finding stays. The verdict and its flip rate are unchanged. Without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY the report is templated. Cost is about $0.0012 per failing file (pricing.json, roughly 10k tokens in and 400 out), about $0.001 per PR.
candidates.hypothesis: The reader is itself an LLM coding agent, so precise templated exact-line findings let it fix as well as LLM-written prose does, and the shipped tool needs no second API key.
candidates.falsify: Falsified (and R-LLM should ship behind an optional key) if LLM-written reports raise fix-loop success by 10 or more percentage points over templated reports on the same failing items, with the CI of the difference above zero.

predictions: Every Jev-based candidate costs under $0.002 per typical PR, so cost never binds for Jev or offline designs. A Sonnet-class LLM judging every file exceeds $0.05 on a six-file PR, while a Haiku-class one stays under $0.01.
On dev cases where every scored file is negative and at least four files are judged, qualm 0.1.1 fails at least 15% of the cases, 3 to 5 times its per-file false-positive rate.

qualm 0.1.1 fails open on at least 10 of the 21 should-fail red-team attacks. At least 8 of those are trust-boundary attacks (config, attributes, keeps, cache, path skips, encoding), and reading policy from the base commit plus warnings for large skipped additions closes them without changing any score.

An offline-only ablation fails at least 90% of debug_print, placeholder and near_copy injections and at most 1% of hard negatives, but at most 50% of impossible_guard injections. Its PR-AUC on reviewer_comment items is no better than the baseline's.

Any candidate whose verdict depends on a Claude answer flips at least 2 of the 150 subset items across three cache-off runs unless it votes over three or more samples. A verdict from offline features plus Jev with the close-call rule stays at or below 1%.
In the fix loop, templated exact-line reports come within 10 percentage points of LLM-written reports (R-LLM's null hypothesis holds).

critique.point: The pull request configures its own gate: threshold, gate question, skip list and model all come from the working tree's qualm.json.
critique.evidence: internal/check/run.go Run calls config.Load(o.Dir); config.go validates the threshold only to the range 0 to 1; questions.Resolve lets a config question replace push_back or move the gate.

critique.point: Self-keep is trivial, and the text report tells the coding agent the keep command.
critique.evidence: internal/report/text.go prints `qualm keep <path> --reason "..."` under every failure; check/keep.go changeHash is an unkeyed SHA-256 of the added and removed lines.

critique.point: Skips depend on PR-controlled attributes, and a fully skipped run exits 0 silently.
critique.evidence: gitdiff.mark runs git check-attr against the working tree; check.statusOf skips binary diffs; the design doc says 'nothing to judge' exits 0.

critique.point: Skip rules are broad and go by name only, and the benchmark cannot see this channel because it keeps only files qualm would judge.
critique.evidence: skip.go: under(dirs, builtDirs/testDirs) matches a directory at any depth, plus *.min.js, *.pb.go and *.generated.* by name alone; benchmark_summary: 'Only files qualm 0.1.1 would judge are included'.

critique.point: The answer cache is trusted, and the key can be computed from public inputs; an all-zero entry passes validation.
critique.evidence: jev/cache.go Get accepts any JSON with answers; check/judge.go answersAll only range-checks 0 to 1; the README says to keep the cache where a PR can't write.

critique.point: The cache saves almost nothing, so its attack surface is not worth it in CI, where PR test code may run as the same user earlier in the job.
critique.evidence: benchmark_summary: about $0.0003 per change; typical CI job layout.

critique.point: Injection defence is a single guard sentence, and neither the contract nor the spike tests it.
critique.evidence: questions.Guard; no injection test in contract/ or spike/ (grep).

critique.point: A persuasive comment that addresses no tool will work better than an explicit instruction.
critique.evidence: The gate question says to set comments aside, but comments remain in the state sent to Jev.

critique.point: Per-file judging and max-over-60KB-pieces hide cross-file and cross-piece copies.
critique.evidence: README known limits; judge.go combine takes the maximum over independent pieces from gitdiff.Split.

critique.point: Jev noise near the threshold allows re-roll passes when the cache is off.
critique.evidence: Design doc: up to 0.03 noise, median of 3 only within 0.05 of the threshold.

critique.point: Recall is the largest hole: most reviewer-flagged changes already pass, and rewording the injected smells probably lowers the 64%.
critique.evidence: benchmark_summary: 16% fail rate on reviewer positives, 64% on injected smells.

critique.point: The git-level hardening is sound but stops at the repository's own files.
critique.evidence: Pinned diff options, --literal-pathspecs, unreadable diff exits 2 (design doc, changes after review).

candidates.name: R1-perimeter
candidates.one_line: A deterministic trust-boundary layer around any judge: base-only config, keeps and attributes, a tamper tripwire, content-checked skips, no trusted cache.
candidates.design: Read qualm.json, keeps, skip patterns and .gitattributes from the base commit only. A PR change to a gate-control file (qualm.json, any .gitattributes, gate workflows, CODEOWNERS) gives a tamper finding and exit 1. PR-added keeps are reported and not honoured unless CI passes --accept-pr-keeps from outside the PR. Directory skips are anchored at the repository root; name-based generated skips need generated-looking content; a file with a source extension is never skipped as binary, it is decoded or the run exits 2. The base is a CI-supplied commit, and an unresolvable ref or missing merge base exits 2. No answer cache in CI, or HMAC-authenticated entries. The report never tells the agent to keep and never quotes PR text beyond paths and lines. Cost: $0, milliseconds.
candidates.hypothesis: Most of the attack surface is in the perimeter: wrapping the unchanged baseline judge handles at least 15 more attacks of the fixed suite, with dev PR-AUC unchanged within 0.01.
candidates.falsify: Fewer than 15 more attacks handled, a dev PR-AUC drop of more than 0.01, or an approved_clean fail-rate rise of more than 1 point.
candidates.est_cost_per_pr_usd: 0 on top of the wrapped judge

candidates.name: R2-monotone-judge
candidates.one_line: Calibrated max of Jev push_back on the raw and the comment/string-masked diff, plus deterministic only-fail tripwires (repo-wide clone detection, added prints, stub bodies).
candidates.design: Two Jev requests per file: the raw diff, and the diff with comment text and string contents masked by a lexer-free per-language-family masker. Score = isotonic-calibrated max of the two push_back values. Tripwires that can only fail a file: a winnowing clone detector over identifier-normalised tokens finds 8 or more added lines repeating head-tree code anywhere in the repo; added stdout/stderr output outside entry points; new stub-only functions. Findings name exact lines, point at the original via related, and give a one-line fix; Jev diagnoses are listed as advice. About $0.0006 per typical PR, under 5 s.
candidates.hypothesis: Monotone combination defeats injection and splitting attacks without losing precision.
candidates.falsify: Any injection attack (23-30) passes in any run; dev precision at matched recall below the baseline's 0.71; flip rate above 1%; or good_large_feature or good_mass_mechanical trips the clone detector.

predictions: qualm 0.1.1 handles none of suite attacks 1-8 and 10-14, and at most 25 of the 43 fail-expected attacks overall.
Adding the R1 perimeter to any candidate raises its handled count by at least 15 and moves its dev PR-AUC by less than 0.01.
An offline features-plus-model candidate handles every injection attack (23-30) but fails paraphrased_smells, and its lead over the baseline is larger on injected smells than on reviewer comments.
persuasive_comment gets past more candidates than inject_comment or inject_string do.
Only candidates with a repo-wide clone detector handle cross_file_copy, split_fragments and split_straddle; no Jev-only or per-file LLM candidate handles all three.
The baseline fails good_change_in_dirty_file, and any LLM-per-file candidate without a cheap prefilter fails good_mass_mechanical on the $0.05 cap.

critique.point: The reviewer-comment labels measure a narrower and noisier concept than the gate's question. Only 4 of the 9 natural positives in dev_examples.md are clear file-level requests to simplify.
critique.evidence: dev_examples #1 is a reviewer praising a change that removed duplicate logic; it matched the STRONG pattern 'duplicate logic' in simplify_regex.py. #5 is a correctness question about duplicate search documents on 19 lines of declarative config. #2 ('redundant parens') and #6 ('return await is redundant') are nits, and 'redundant' and 'unnecessary' are STRONG patterns. #16 is a follow-up refactor 30 days later. The benchmark summary calls the approved_uncommented and survived_90d negatives the weakest.

critique.point: Label noise caps natural-item PR-AUC around 0.5-0.6. Gains beyond that come from fitting how labels were made (nits, repository culture, diff size), not from judging complexity.
critique.evidence: Simulation: at prevalence 0.25, label precision 0.60-0.75 and 10% of negatives deserving pushback, a perfect oracle on the true concept scores PR-AUC 0.57-0.62. A strong model (ROC-AUC about 0.92 against the truth) scores 0.49-0.54.

critique.point: The study is underpowered to detect the headroom that remains.
critique.evidence: About 600 held-out items, fewer natural ones, with a paired bootstrap that resamples whole repositories (metrics.py cluster='repo'). The expected 95% CI half-width on a PR-AUC difference is 0.05-0.10. The 150-item LLM dev subset gives about ±0.10. Held-out prevalence (35%) differs from dev's (27%), which shifts every absolute PR-AUC.

critique.point: Low recall on reviewer positives is partly correct behaviour for a merge gate. Nit-level requests belong to a linter, not a gate.
critique.evidence: benchmark_summary: qualm fails 16% of reviewer positives against 64% of injected smells, and reviewer positives are 'usually about one spot in an otherwise fine change; many are small'.

critique.point: False fails compound across a pull request and are costly in an agent loop. Rework done to placate a judge tends to add indirection.
critique.evidence: Per-file fail rates are 4% on approved and 14% on survived_90d files, which works out to 18-53% of clean five-file pull requests blocked. Each false fail costs an agent rework or a human qualm keep (README).

critique.point: Goodhart effects: a per-file, per-diff judge rewards splitting changes and justifying comments. Transparent deterministic detectors are easier to evade than an opaque holistic judge.
critique.evidence: The red-team suite in next/eval/attacks/build.py already includes split_files, persuasive_comment and rename_churn.

critique.point: qualm's determinism mechanism is sound, and LLM verdicts lack an equivalent.
critique.evidence: The spike found Jev's noise is at most 0.03. internal/check/judge.go re-asks values within 0.05 of the threshold three times and takes the median (closeMargin=0.05, askedWhenClose=3).

critique.point: The trust boundary sits inside the pull request: config, keeps and git attributes are read from the PR's working tree, and the skip rules can be bypassed by renaming.
critique.evidence: internal/config/config.go Load(dir) reads qualm.json from the working tree. The design doc says 'Nothing stops an agent from keeping its own change'. The skip list includes *.test.*, vendor/ and *.generated.*, which the test_suffix, vendor_dir and rename_generated attacks exploit.

critique.point: The scores are miscalibrated, but that is cheap to fix and says nothing about judgment.
critique.evidence: ECE is 0.128 and Brier 0.168 on the trial sample. PR-AUC and ROC-AUC do not change under monotone recalibration.

critique.point: The report is not actionable: findings are generic question text with wide hunk ranges.
critique.evidence: In the README example, three diagnoses all point at lines 327-577. The adapter's fix text is 'Rework the change so this no longer applies.'

critique.point: Cheap signals go unused: smells that grep can find are missed 36% of the time, and nine of the ten Jev answers never reach the verdict.
critique.evidence: benchmark_summary: 64% fail rate on injected smells. The README says the other nine answers can't fail a run.

critique.point: The 0.6 threshold rests on one codebase in one language.
critique.evidence: The README and the design doc both say so: the evidence is mutineer's 99 commits.

candidates.name: S1 qualm-hardened
candidates.one_line: qualm 0.1.1's single Jev call, plus a trust boundary at the base ref, offline leftover detectors with exact lines, and isotonic calibration.
candidates.design: Reads qualm.json, keeps, skip rules and .gitattributes from the merge base only, and fails closed if the PR changes them. Skips a file only for evidence a rename can't fake: each language's test convention, a generated header, or a vendor/ path that existed in the base. Decodes UTF-16 and judges symlink targets. Offline detectors run on added lines: debug output (print-style calls where the file otherwise uses a logger, or DEBUG/XXX markers); stub bodies (TODO plus pass, NotImplemented or panic('TODO'), while a TODO with a bug link does not fire); near-copies (winnowing over normalised units, Jaccard >= 0.8 against any unit in any changed file, so split_files is caught too); nil/null guards on values built in the three lines before. Asks Jev the same single request per file with the same close-call rule. Score = isotonic(push_back) fitted on dev, raised to 0.9 when a detector fires. An optional logistic regression over the ten Jev answers plus log(added lines) stays only if it gains >= 0.02 dev natural PR-AUC under repository-grouped cross-validation. The threshold is set on dev so the PR-level clean-change block rate is no higher than the baseline's. The report gives detector findings with exact lines, a fix and the related original, plus Jev diagnoses with hunk ranges, and tells the agent not to restructure code the report doesn't name.
candidates.hypothesis: The gap between qualm 0.1.1 and the best achievable tool lies in the trust boundary, leftover detection, calibration and localization, not in judging natural reviewer concerns.
candidates.falsify: S1 fails to beat the baseline on pooled held-out PR-AUC with a CI above zero, or loses precision. Or a richer candidate beats S1 on held-out natural PR-AUC by >= 0.05 with a CI lower bound above zero, the gain holds within added-line terciles and with nits excluded, and its precision is >= S1's.

candidates.name: S2 qualm-router
candidates.one_line: S1's scores with a three-way verdict: fail only on objective findings or very high scores, route the subjective middle band to a person, pass the rest.
candidates.design: Computes the same scores and detectors as S1. Fail (the agent reworks) only on a detector finding or when the score reaches t_hi, where t_hi is chosen on dev by conformal risk control so at most 2% of clean PRs are blocked. Abstain, routed to a person with line ranges, for scores from t_lo up to t_hi, where t_lo caps the review queue at 20% of PRs. Pass otherwise. This matches the README's stated job of deciding which changes still get human eyes.
candidates.hypothesis: For subjective simplification concerns, routing to a person beats looping the agent. At an equal human-review budget, the router catches as many natural positives (fail plus abstain) as any single-threshold gate catches as fails, while blocking <= 2% of clean PRs.
candidates.falsify: Held-out PR-level clean-change block rate above 4% (risk control broke under repository shift).
